purpose: Restores the dev/test OTP flow for Hugging Face Spaces by returning the generated OTP as devOtp in the /auth/send-otp response and making email delivery best-effort, and removes all per-route auth rate limiters per the maintainer's directive.
riskRationale: The two core changes are applied unconditionally in every environment: generated OTPs are returned in a public API response (full account takeover if the API is reachable in production, where NODE_ENV defaults to production on most platforms) and all auth rate limiters are removed, leaving verify-otp with zero brute-force protection. Additionally, making sendEmail never reject silently defeats BullMQ's 3-attempt retry for worker-sent notification emails, turning transient SMTP outages into permanent email loss.
breakingChanges: OTP returned as devOtp in the /auth/send-otp response in all environments, including production (account-takeover vector)
Per-route auth rate limiters removed from /register, /send-otp, /verify-otp, /refresh; only the global 600-per-15-min limiter remains (no OTP brute-force or account-spam protection)

sendEmail no longer rejects on SMTP/Resend failure, so callers relying on rejection (e.g., BullMQ worker job retries for notification emails) will no longer retry and failures are only visible as warn logs

text: The refactor is mechanically clean: rate-limit code is removed thoroughly (including the in-memory otpRateMap, its setInterval cleanup, and all limiter middleware), the OTP stays available as devOtp, and the new email test verifying the best-effort contract is focused and well-written. However, the two headline changes — unconditionally returning devOtp and unconditionally removing auth rate limiting — are security regressions if applied in production, and the non-throwing sendEmail silently defeats BullMQ's retry semantics for worker-sent notification emails while making the 'OTP email sent' log in the worker misleading.

reasoning: Direction matches the maintainer's directive and the PR description, but the two security-sensitive changes must be environment-gated before merge: gate devOtp by isProd (auth.controller.ts:135) and keep auth rate limiters when NODE_ENV=production (auth.routes.ts). The sendEmail retry-semantics issue additionally needs a maintainer decision on which callers should be best-effort, so auto-fixing all items safely is not guaranteed.

message: Good focused test: exercises both the SMTP-reject path (asserts sendEmail resolves and logs a warning containing the error message) and the success path (asserts no warning), using vi.hoisted to control sendMail before the dynamic import. This directly verifies the new best-effort contract introduced by the PR.

The rate-limit removal is thorough: checkOtpRateLimit, the in-memory otpRateMap, its constants, and the setInterval cleanup are removed together, eliminating dead code and a source of unbounded memory growth with no dangling state or timers.
Well-written documentation that clearly explains the devOtp-in-response behavior, the frontend NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_OTP flag needed to surface it, and the rationale for removing rate limits.

sendOtp unconditionally returns the generated OTP as devOtp in the response for every environment, including NODE_ENV=production. Since send-otp is a public endpoint, anyone who knows a user's email can call it, read the real OTP from the response, and then call /auth/verify-otp to log in as that user — full account takeover. The frontend already gates UI display on NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_OTP==='true' (frontend/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx:61), and isProd already exists at line 19, so gating the backend value is safe.
suggestion: Only include devOtp when not in production (reuse the existing isProd const at line 19), and update the sendOtp test to set NODE_ENV accordingly instead of asserting the field is always present.

message: All auth rate limiters were removed unconditionally: registerLimiter (5/15min), otpLimiter (3/5min on /send-otp and /verify-otp), and refreshLimiter (10/min). /verify-otp is an unauthenticated endpoint that issues access/refresh tokens and now has zero brute-force protection — a 6-digit OTP (~900k combinations) can be exhausted with parallel requests within the 5-minute TTL since verifyOtp does not invalidate the record on a failed guess. /send-otp also becomes an unlimited email/DB amplification vector and /register is open to mass-account spam. This is a production security regression regardless of the dev-testing intent.
suggestion: Gate limiter usage by environment: keep express-rate-limit applied when NODE_ENV==='production' (or behind a dedicated AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED flag) and disable only in dev/test, mirroring the env-gating used for devOtp. At minimum, document this as a known security tradeoff for the HF Space deployment.

message: The catch-all makes sendEmail never reject, which silently defeats the BullMQ retry mechanism: lib/queue.ts sets defaultJobOptions.attempts=3, so worker jobs (notification.worker.ts:366,388,424,690,729,757) previously re-ran on transient SMTP failure and now complete 'successfully' with the email never delivered. Meanwhile notification.worker.ts:373 logs 'OTP email sent' even when the send failed, and failures in opportunities.service.ts:440 and admin.service.ts:237 are masked as warn logs. This turns transient SMTP outages into silent permanent email loss for application-accepted/rejected/suspension notifications.
suggestion: Don't swallow errors for all callers. The OTP/auth path already wraps sendEmail gracefully (auth.controller.ts:128 .catch on enqueueOtpEmail and the fallback catch in auth.service.ts:84-95), so keep sendEmail throwing for the worker and other callers to preserve BullMQ retries and truthful success logs, or add an explicit option e.g. sendEmail(..., { bestEffort: true }) used only by the auth OTP path. At minimum, make the worker log reflect actual delivery success.

message: Now that sendEmail never throws, the try/catch around the direct-send fallback in enqueueOtpEmail is dead code — the catch at line 91 can never fire. The same unreachable handling applies to the .catch(...) on sendEmail in opportunities.service.ts:440 and the try/catch in admin.service.ts:237.
suggestion: Remove the now-unreachable catch in enqueueOtpEmail (and optionally tidy the other call sites) since sendEmail's failure path is fully handled internally, or keep the guard if sendEmail regains throwing behavior per the retry concern above.
